newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end higher ahead of FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end higher ahead of FOMC meeting.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed higher ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting which is expected to result in a 25-basis-point U.S. rate increase, traders and analysts said.
"We're just sitting here waiting for a 25-basis-point rate hike," one Eurodollar futures trader said.

June T-bonds and September Eurodollars set the day's highs in the final minutes of pit trade, possibly gearing up for a relief rally after FOMC meeting, traders said. Both June bonds and most Eurodollar contracts closed near the daily highs.
The FOMC has not set a time for an announcement.
Some traders were speculating on the time of the FOMC's announcement, considering the U.S. Treasury department is scheduled to auction $17.25 billion two-year notes on Tuesday.
"Most people are looking for a rate announcement after the auction results," one bond futures trader at a major U.S. bank said.
Several traders agreed, adding that an announcement is likely to occur around the usual time of 1300 to 1330 CST (1900 to 1930 GMT).
"The only real surprise about tomorrow is when the FOMC will make the announcement," another trader said.
"I mean, how aggressive will the bidding for two-year notes be when the FOMC is meeting?" he said.
Traders said June T-bonds' intraday push to 109-00, which is roughly equivalent to a long bond yield of 6.95 percent, could lead the contract to the 109-08/32 to 109-10/32 area.
"That would be the pivot point," one trader said.
Meanwhile, September Eurodollars steadily inched up to 93.835, near resistance at 93.84. Further resistance is at 93.89.
Buying activity was too spotty and light to create much momentum, they said.
In the 10-year note futures market, an offer of 1,000 June contracts was pulled due to lack of interest in the pit.
"It's been painfully quiet," one trader said.
A FOMC decision to either leave rates unchanged or raise short-term rates by more than 50 basis points would shatter the market's firm tone and spark a heavy selloff, traders said.

Support is seen at 108-16/32 or 108-20/32 in June bonds, or the seven-percent yield level, and at 93.79, the double bottom and yearly low, for September Eurodollars. Further support is seen at 93.69 and 93.60.

At the end of pit trade, June T-bonds were up 08/32 at 108-31/32, 10-year notes were 05/32 higher at 106-20/32, muni bonds were up 03/32 at 113-10/32, September T-bills were up 0.015 at 94.37 and September Eurodollars were up 0.02 at 93.83.
